transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just can't keep my mind on my actual experiments anymore. It's becoming a real problem at work. I'll be in the middle of an important grant call or a safety meeting, and I'll notice something completely unrelated—like a pump vibrating in the lab, or a student's random side comment, or even just some odd peak in an old data spectrum. 

And suddenly I'm off chasing that one little thing for hours. I just completely drop what I'm supposed to be doing, and the work that everyone actually needs from me just falls apart.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility since childhood, or is this a recent change?

No, it's definitely a recent change. I never really had this issue growing up or, you know, earlier in my career. I'd say this has been going on for about seven months now. It really started right around the time I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
During these past seven months, have you found that you need much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Yes, actually. It's... it's been pretty extreme. Most nights I'm only sleeping maybe two or three hours. I'll just crash on the couch with my laptop still open, and then I'm awake again. But the weird thing is, I don't feel tired at all. I wake up completely sharp and just ready to get back to work. It honestly feels like sleeping is just this inefficient interruption to everything I need to get done.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had a period in your life where you felt persistently down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I've never really felt down or depressed like that. I mean, I've had stressful periods, sure, but I've always been pretty focused and engaged with my work and life. I've never lost interest in things or felt that kind of persistent low mood.
Have these issues led to severe consequences at work, such as being placed on leave, facing formal disciplinary action, or being at risk of losing your job?

Yeah, it actually has. My department has had to step in recently on decisions that I usually handle myself. I guess... well, there were missed priorities, and my scheduling got really confused. My supervision of the team got pretty strained, too. It reached a point where they told me I was starting to put the whole project, and even our lab safety expectations, at risk. So, yes, it's definitely causing some serious problems for my job.
During these past several months, have you felt like your thoughts are racing or moving much faster than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My thoughts don't feel like they're racing or moving too fast. I mean... I'm thinking about my work and my projects a lot, obviously, but my mind just feels clear and focused on what I need to get done. It doesn't feel out of control or faster than normal to me.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized, high, or wired like this?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I've always been a dedicated worker, and I've definitely had times where I was productive, but never anything quite like this. These past seven months have just been... different. I've never felt this kind of constant, intense energy before.
